comment: Known semantic gaps per utility, each a short sentence naming the option or behavior. Lanes update their own utilities.

ls: SELinux contexts (-Z, --context) print `?` and the ACL/context marker after the mode string is never shown: there is no xattr API (needs `system.posix_acl_access`/`security.selinux`/`security.capability` reads for the `+`/`.` marker, `-Z`, and the `ca=` color).
Names sort bytewise (the C locale); a UTF-8 locale's `strcoll` order (test_ls_sort_dot_first_utf8_locale, the UTF-8 branch of test_ls_order_time_breaks_ties_by_name) is not implemented.
Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset (`EST5`, `<+03>-3`); zone names and DST rules need a tz database (`%Z` shows the TZ abbreviation as written).
Terminal width comes from COLUMNS or 80: there is no TIOCGWINSZ query, so a terminal's real width is not used.
Stdout write failures are invisible (`ls: write error: ...`, exit 2: test_write_error, test_dired_write_error), see the runtime flush blocker in requests.md.
Non-UTF-8 operands cannot be passed (xsh rejects non-UTF-8 argv); non-UTF-8 entry names are quoted from their raw bytes but sorted and matched by their lossy text.

Directories are read eagerly: `ls -l /proc/self/fd` stats the descriptor that read the directory after it is closed (test_ls_proc_self_fd_no_errors, a regression from the old applet's accidental pass). Needs a lazy `fs.children` that keeps the directory open while entries are stat'ed. Terminal width: `unix.window_size` now exists, so ls can query it.
stty: Integer arguments follow the uutils tests' overflow wording (`Value too large for defined data type`); GNU 9.4 on the host prints `Numerical result out of range`. One constant (`OVERFLOW_TEXT`) in core/stty.xsh flips it if the 9.12 source says otherwise.
Size suffixes of GNU `integer_arg` (`1k`, `2b`) are not accepted; such arguments are `invalid integer argument`.
Fractional speeds (`9600.49`) are accepted as the uutils tests require; GNU 9.4 on the host rejects them as `invalid ispeed`.
Arguments after `--` are settings; GNU 9.4 silently ignores them.

A terminal that keeps other state than requested (a pty drops parity and sizes other than 8 bits) is reported as `unable to perform all requested operations`; GNU 9.4 reports `Invalid argument` for some of those from tcsetattr itself, which `unix.set_tty_attrs` does not raise.
`-g` prints 32 control characters like glibc, but the kernel keeps 19: a saved state that sets later ones is applied and then refused as GNU does.
more: Commands are read a line at a time (RETURN ends each): there is no unbuffered or timed stdin read, so single-key paging, Ctrl-C handling and window-resize redraws are missing (request: an `io.stdin_read`/`unix.read_fd` primitive).
A pipe on standard input is printed in full instead of paged: the commands would have to come from /dev/tty, which has no read primitive.
Non-UTF-8 operands cannot be passed (xsh rejects non-UTF-8 argv): test_more::test_more_non_utf8_paths.

test_more::test_invalid_file_perms needs a non-root user and the lowercase `permission denied` of Rust's ErrorKind; the applet prints strerror text (`Permission denied`) and root can read the file anyway.
-u strips underline and bold overstrikes; there is no terminfo standout mode to switch to otherwise.
who: Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset (`EST5`, `<+03>-3`); zone names and DST rules need a tz database, and an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).

`who -b` and the boot record synthesized for a default utmp file without one derive the boot time from `unix.uptime_seconds` (whole seconds), so it can differ from GNU's by a second at a minute boundary.
`--lookup` canonicalizes nothing: `dns` has no canonical name (getaddrinfo AI_CANONNAME), so numeric hosts pass and a host name fails with an explicit message (request: `dns.canonical`).

test_who::test_too_many_args and the two test_who::*_piped_to_dev_full tests assert clap and uutils wording; the applet prints GNU 9.4's `extra operand 'u'` and `who: write error: No space left on device`.
users: Sessions of the default utmp file are checked for live pids (`process.kill` with signal 0) as gnulib does; an explicit FILE is listed as written.
uptime: Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset; an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).
`-p` and `-s` are procps options (not GNU coreutils); they are implemented because the uutils tests exercise them.
test_uptime::test_uptime_with_extra_argument asserts clap wording (`unexpected value 'b'`); the applet prints GNU's `extra operand 'b'`.
pinky: Time zones: TZ is read as UTC or a fixed POSIX offset; an unset TZ reads as UTC instead of /etc/localtime (request: a local-time primitive).

Accounts come from /etc/passwd (`lib.auth`, or XSH_PASSWD_FILE) rather than NSS, and `user.lookup` has no GECOS field (request: `gecos` on `user.lookup`). XSH_UTMP_FILE replaces /var/run/utmp for tests.
`--lookup` canonicalizes nothing: `dns` has no canonical name (getaddrinfo AI_CANONNAME), so numeric hosts pass and a host name fails with an explicit message (request: `dns.canonical`).
date: French `%b` abbreviations retain glibc/GNU punctuation (`févr.`, `janv.`, `déc.`), while uutils' ICU-based locale expectations omit the trailing dot. Known residuals: `test_date::test_locale_abbreviated_month_names` and `test_date::test_locale_names_for_several_dates_in_one_run`; keep GNU-compatible output.
mkfifo: test_mkfifo::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_bad_operator expects a source caret; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `mkfifo: invalid mode`.
mknod: test_mknod::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_bad_operator expects a source caret; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `mknod: invalid mode`.
test_mknod::test_mknod_invalid_arg expects clap's `unexpected argument` wording; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `mknod: unrecognized option` and its standard help hint.
pathchk: test_pathchk::test_no_args expects clap's required-arguments wording; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `pathchk: missing operand` and its standard help hint.
pwd: For a deleted working directory, GNU coreutils 9.12 reports `couldn't find directory entry in ‘..’ with matching i-node`; uutils' test_pwd::test_deleted_dir expects `failed to get current directory: No such file or directory`, which XSH follows.
readlink: test_readlink::test_no_args expects clap's required-arguments wording; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `readlink: missing operand` and its standard help hint.
shred: test_shred::diagnostics::test_snippet_points_at_the_unknown_unit and test_shred::diagnostics::test_snippet_underlines_a_size_with_no_number expect source carets; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `shred: invalid file size` without a snippet.
truncate: test_truncate::diagnostics::test_snippet_counts_the_mode_character_before_the_size expects a source caret; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `truncate: Invalid number` without a snippet.
test_truncate::test_error_filename_only expects clap's required-arguments block; GNU coreutils 9.12 prints `truncate: you must specify either '--size' or '--reference'` and its standard help hint.
mkdir: ACL setup fails before the applet runs on this host filesystem: test_mkdir::test_mkdir_acl and test_mkdir::test_mkdir_acl_inheritance_with_restrictive_mask get EOPNOTSUPP (`Operation not supported`) while setting the ACL.
test_mkdir::test_no_arg expects clap's required-arguments wording; GNU 9.12 prints `mkdir: missing operand` and its standard help hint, which the applet follows.
test_mkdir::test_version_no_path expects the `mkdir (uutils coreutils)` branding; the applet uses GNU 9.12 version branding.
rm: Recursive permission traversal differs in test_rm::test_inaccessible_dir_recursive, test_rm::test_only_first_error_recursive, test_rm::test_recursive_remove_unreadable_subdir, test_rm::test_remove_inaccessible_dir, test_rm::test_rm_directory_not_executable, and test_rm::test_rm_directory_not_writable: fs.walk reports the inaccessible top-level directory or stops before the denied descendant, so errors name the parent (or removal fails) instead of following GNU/uutils behavior for the child.
test_rm::test_rm_recursive_very_deep_hierarchy exceeds the directory walker's file-descriptor limit (`Too many open files`); the uutils test then also stack-overflows while cleaning up the deep tree.
rmdir: test_rmdir::test_no_arg expects clap's required-arguments wording; GNU 9.12 prints `rmdir: missing operand` and its standard help hint, which the applet follows.
touch: test_touch::test_touch_invalid_timestamp_leading_multibyte_char expects a literal euro sign in the invalid-date diagnostic; under LC_ALL=C GNU quotes its UTF-8 bytes as `\342\202\254`, which the applet follows.
test_touch::test_touch_mtime_dst_fails passes a nonexistent local time in a DST gap; time.parse has no timezone transition rules to reject it, so touch succeeds where the test expects an error.
test_touch::test_touch_set_date_wrong_format expects uutils' `Unable to parse date: 2005-43-21`; GNU 9.12 prints `touch: invalid date format '2005-43-21'`, which the applet follows.
getty: getty -h/--flow-control, -L/--local-line, -m/--extract-baud, -w/--wait-cr, and -t/--timeout are explicitly rejected because terminal line control, modem baud detection, CR-wait, and timed login are unavailable; these options match util-linux getty's host help, and uutils has no getty tests.
ifdown: ifdown -v/--verbose is explicitly rejected because verbose hook and network-operation reporting is not implemented; ifupdown is not installed on the host for a native comparison, and uutils has no ifdown tests.
ifup: ifup -v/--verbose is explicitly rejected because verbose hook and network-operation reporting is not implemented; ifupdown is not installed on the host for a native comparison, and uutils has no ifup tests.
pstree: pstree -c/--compact-not, -l/--long, -t/--thread-names, -T/--hide-threads, and -h/-H highlighting are explicitly rejected because subtree controls, terminal-width-aware rendering, thread display, and process highlighting are unavailable; these flags match procps-ng pstree help, and uutils has no pstree tests.
